headline: 2 Bangladeshis injured in Dammam airport attack
summary: The attack on King Fahd International Airport left two Indian nationals dead and eight others injured, including two Bangladeshis.
details: Two Bangladeshi expatriates were injured in an attack targeting King Fahd International Airport in Dammam, Saudi Arabia.
The attack, which occurred on Wednesday night, reportedly killed two Indian nationals and left eight people injured.
The injured include two Bangladeshis, two Indians, two Yemenis, one Saudi national, and one Nepali.
The injured Bangladeshis have been identified as Sajal Chandra Das from Cumilla and Mohammad Abdur Rahim from Noakhali.
According to the expatriates’ welfare ministry, both men are currently receiving treatment at the Saudi German Hospital in Dammam.

headline: Over 2,300 tourists evacuated from Sajek amid clashes and gunfire
summary: Security forces conducted a joint operation to rescue stranded travelers after a road blockade and reported gunfights in Rangamati's Baghaichhari upazila.
details: More than 2,300 tourists were evacuated from the Sajek road in Rangamati’s Baghaichhari upazila today after being stranded by a road blockade and subsequent clashes.
The Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) stated that the army and police conducted a joint security operation to ensure the safe passage of the travelers.
According to ISPR, blockaders at Gangaram Bazar began throwing bricks and stones at law enforcers and tourists around 10:45 am, leading to a baton charge to disperse the crowd.
ISPR further alleged that armed UPDF members fired 30 to 40 rounds at security forces and tourists, prompting the army to return fire in self-defence to protect the civilians.
Rangamati Superintendent of Police Muhammad Abdur Rakib confirmed that five army personnel and two police members were injured in the incident, though no tourists were harmed.
The blockade, which began at 6:00 am, involved placing logs across the road at several points, including Ujo Bazar, trapping a convoy of tourists returning from Sajek Valley.
UPDF spokesperson Angya Marma has denied the reports of a gunfight, claiming instead that security personnel fired shots to break up a peaceful road blockade by local residents.
The situation was reported to be under control after 1:00 pm following the evacuation of the tourists.
caption:
Over 2,300 tourists were stranded and evacuated under army protection after gunfire broke out during a road blockade in Sajek.
